title: Brigade Enterprises Ltd - 532929 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Brigade Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 36% (from 28%) on real estate margin recovery, though net sales fell 5% to INR1,061 crore.
summary.overview:
Consolidated revenue was INR1,179 crore with EBITDA of INR425 crore, and PAT of INR217 crore (up 37% YoY). Real estate EBITDA margin recovered to 21% from 12%, driven by recognition of higher-margin projects, while realisation rose 21% YoY to INR14,256 per sq ft. Q1 had no launches; the Morgan Heights relaunch was stalled after SEIAA revoked its environmental clearance, and management cut that project from the launch schedule. FY27 presales guidance of INR9,000 crore was reiterated, with launches back-ended and the launch pipeline trimmed to about 9.36 million sq ft for the rest of FY27.</overview>

segments.name: Real Estate
segments.commentary: Net sales INR707 crore and EBITDA INR150 crore (21% margin vs 12%); realisation INR14,256 per sq ft (+21% YoY) on price increases and mix shift to higher-value homes. Q1 had no new launches; Q1 presales were about INR1,050 crore per analyst question.

segments.name: Leasing (commercial office)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR328 crore (+9% YoY), EBITDA INR230 crore at 70% margin; operational GLA 8 million sq ft, occupancy 88%, gross leasing 0.22 million sq ft in Q1, rental collections 99%. Office revenue cited as INR200 crore.

segments.name: Hospitality (BHVL)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR144 crore, EBITDA INR45 crore; ADR +7%, occupancy 76% (from 74.5%), RevPAR and EBITDA up about 9%. West Asia conflict cut event/MICE business by about 10%.

segments.name: Retail (Orion Mall)
segments.commentary: Footfalls +11% YoY, retail sales +35% YoY, anchor retailer sales +64%, F&B +46%, electronics +33%, cinema admissions +20%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales guidance of INR9,000 crore reiterated; management says sales run-rate per quarter should rise as launches start from Q2.
Launch pipeline for the rolling four quarters is 12.36 million sq ft (residential 12.4 million sq ft at about INR13,400 crore GDV; commercial about 4.03 million sq ft), excluding Morgan Heights.
Within this, about 9.36 million sq ft is planned for the rest of FY27 (Q2 about 2.36 million sq ft, H2 about 7 million sq ft) and about 3 million sq ft slips into Q1 FY28.
Hyderabad Neopolis 2 (about 2 million sq ft) is now expected in Q2; Whitefield-Hoskote is now a Q3 launch; Hyderabad launch pulled forward to Q3 or earlier.
Commercial leasing revenue expected to grow at about 20% CAGR over the next 5 to 6 years; about 6 million sq ft of commercial space to come into the market mainly in FY30.
Operating contribution margin improvement of 5% to 6% expected to be largely retained through FY27; management expects margins to move into the 20s, from late teens at year end last year.
Debt-equity to stay well under 1x, with capex and BD funded first from internal accruals.
BHVL to add 1,700 keys in pipeline, targeting 3,300 keys by FY31; Courtyard by Marriott Chennai WTC (45 keys) to launch in FY27.
capex_capacity: Launch pipeline: Q1 had none; Morgan Heights (about 0.7 million sq ft unsold, attributable value about INR650 crore) removed from launch schedule pending High Court and SEIAA resolution.

Commercial pipeline launched in Q1 about 4 million sq ft across Bengaluru and Hyderabad (Brigade HRC Atrium, an industrial block, Brigade United, Cauvery, Orion Mall Hyderabad), all to be held, none for sale.
WTC Bengaluru: about 1.13 million sq ft building, Brigade holds 0.71 million sq ft, about 50% leased, about 375,000 sq ft vacant.
Upcoming commercial: 2.6 million sq ft Bengaluru (about 65%), 1.3 million sq ft Chennai (about 31%), 0.2 million sq ft Kochi.
Capex for commercial projects to be spent over the next 4 to 5 years; per sq ft capex quoted at INR4,000 to INR10,000 (construction cost, excluding land).

Land bank about 56 to 57 million sq ft, which includes the launch pipeline. Kengeri land parcel in litigation; KIADB 75-acre Devanahalli parcel residential component reduced to about 3 to 4 lakh sq ft.
demand_pricing: Pan-India residential sales down 6% YoY in April-June (Anarock); Bengaluru and Hyderabad among the only major cities with sales growth.
Q1 business development: INR2,400 crore GDV across 2.7 million sq ft, mainly Hyderabad.
Office leasing demand led by industrial and manufacturing, flexible workspace and life sciences; GCCs 58% of gross leasing; IT/ITES 26% of portfolio.
WTC Bengaluru: large-occupier RFPs (1-2 lakh sq ft) postponed due to West Asia crisis; leasing shifting to 20,000 to 40,000 sq ft deals; mark-to-market rent increase of 10% to 15%.

Hospitality: domestic corporate, weddings and social demand offset weaker international travel; Kochi (Four Points rebranded to Courtyard by Marriott) occupancy back in the 70s in Q2, ADR uplift expected at 15% to 20%.
